m: The {Magician} in the {Basement} of the {Lake} cabin waves his wand over a scruffy *sheep*, and it turns **beautiful**: silky wool, sparkly hooves, a tiara. A *big man* watching gasps and begs for a turn. One wave and he is **beautiful** too, in a ballgown, twirling so hard he knocks the magician into a laundry basket.

The {Shepherd} climbs a *lookout* on the {Rooftop} of the {Stadium} and spots another shepherd on a lookout across the pitch. They wave at **each other**, then shout at **each other**, then throw sandwiches at **each other**. The fans swivel back and forth as if watching tennis, until the two shepherds blow kisses at **each other**.

The {Juggler} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Yen Exchange} into the arms of a *watcher* with eyes all over his coat. He can **see** everything: the coins in her pockets, the mouse under the counter, her breakfast. 'I **see** you,' all the eyes say together. She juggles faster, but he **sees** every ball.

The {Baker} falls through the {Trapdoor} of the {Lake} pier and is swallowed **by** a giant fish. Inside, his *shirt* is nibbled **by** minnows and his hat is stolen **by** an eel. He wraps himself in an old cow *hide* as a disguise, but is spotted **by** a duck. Everything happens to him; he does nothing at all.

The {Lifeguard} pops out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Beach} tower swinging a *sickle* and harvests a field of ice lollies growing in the sand. The **benefit** is instant: free lollies for every swimmer. Kids cheer, seagulls cheer, and even the crabs get a **benefit**, a tiny lolly each, which they carry off sideways.

The {Sheriff} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Funfair} ghost train and meets a *standing person* holding a giant *cross* like a question mark. '**What** is this?' asks the sheriff. '**What**?' asks the person. '**What** what?' Ghosts lean out of the dark, all whispering **what**, until nobody knows **what** anybody means.

The {Ghost} rises out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Car Park} carrying *two planks* and lays them across **two** parking spaces. On top he parks **two** bicycles, **two** prams and **two** wheelbarrows. A driver honks angrily. The ghost splits neatly in **two**, and both halves honk back even louder.

The {Dentist} sits in the {Basement} of the {Jungle} *temple* on a bench made of *bamboo*, holding ticket number nine million. She has **to wait**. She **waits** while the bamboo grows through the ceiling, **waits** while monkeys raise families, **waits** while her beard reaches the floor. At last a monk calls out: number two.

The {Chef} in the {Basement} of the {Mansion} runs a strange kitchen where every oven **produces** a *newborn* animal: a lamb, a chick, a baby elephant. Ding! Another one. The basement fills with squeaking babies, and the ovens won't switch off; they keep **producing** more until the whole mansion is a zoo.

The {Hunter} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Warehouse} into a *guard post*, where a guard blocks two doors. 'Left **or** right? Tea **or** coffee? Cake **or** tickling?' The hunter can't choose. He tries both doors at once and gets stuck in the middle, still muttering **or**, **or**, **or**.

The {Shepherd} on the {Rooftop} of the {Inn} chops a pile of *firewood*, and every log that splits pops out something **new**: a shiny kettle, a brand-**new** hat, a sheep still in its packaging. The guests stampede up the stairs to swap their old socks for **new** ones that still smell of the shop.

The {Juggler} in the {Basement} of the {Beach} house ties a *coiled rope* round her waist and starts to juggle her own **self**: she flings herself up, catches herself, flings again. Neighbours press their noses to the window. 'Who is helping you?' 'Nobody! Just my**self**!' she cries, upside down.

The {Jockey} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and grabs a *standing knife* like a joystick. Now she can **control** everything: tilt left and the bees fly left, tilt right and they swerve right. She makes them spell her name in the sky. The queen bee wants **control** back and bites her finger.

The {Sheriff} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Funfair} beside a giant inflatable *torso* that bounces in the wind. It is a whole **body** with no arms or head, and children trampoline on its belly. The sheriff lassoes it, but the **body** bounces off over the dodgems, dragging him behind it like a kite.

The {Gardener} in the {Basement} of the {Warehouse} plants one seed, and *fruit* explodes from the ceiling: apples, mangoes, melons the size of cars. The **fruit** keeps falling, rolling, squishing. She surfs a wave of jam to the stairs while forklifts skid in the juice, and the whole place smells of **fruit** salad.

The {Juggler} on the {Rooftop} of the {Piazza} juggles a giant *plus sign*. Every time she catches it, she has **to add** something: one ball, then a teapot, then a pigeon, then a scooter. The crowd keeps shouting '**Add** more!' until she is juggling the cathedral bell and the tower is leaning.

The {Shepherd} lies on the {Rooftop} of the {Beach} chalet as the sun sinks into the sea. A *bird nest* on the chimney empties as every bird takes off flying **west** into the sunset. His sheep follow, paddling **west** after the sun, bleating goodnight, until only their fluffy tails bob on the orange water.

The {Sailor} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Beehive}, *tearing* pages out of her logbook and holding each one up. '**This**! And **this**!' she cries, waving maps of islands made of honey. The ripping noise sends the bees into a frenzy. Finally she tears out a page with one word on it, **this**, and everyone cheers.

The {Yogi} falls through the {Trapdoor} of the {Ice Rink} and lands on the *moon*, which has rolled down from the sky to go skating. The **moon** spins pirouettes, wobbles and crashes into the boards. In the end the yogi has to push the **moon** back up into the sky with a very long hockey stick.

The {Hunter} shoots out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Water Park} on a slide shaped like a huge pink *tongue*. A *small speech bubble* floats over his head as he starts a **speech**: 'Friends, swimmers, inflatable bananas!' Every splash interrupts the **speech**, so he finishes it underwater, bubbles rising.

The {Hunter} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Hut} with a pot and its *fitted lid*, which refuse **to join**. He pushes; they spring apart. He sits on it: click! They **join**, and suddenly everything wants **to join**: the stairs lock together, his boots glue together, and he hops away like a kangaroo.

The {Hunter} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Waiting Room} and finds a *fence* inside another *fence*, a box within a box. He walks round and round between them hunting for the exit, and always **returns** to the same plastic chair. He tries again: he **returns**. One last try, and he **returns** holding a sandwich.

The {Tailor} pops up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Hut} into a *temple*, where a *cow* is being dressed for a **special** day. She stitches it a golden suit with **special** buttons and a hat full of bells. The cow parades down the aisle while monks throw petals, feeling very **special** indeed.

The {Dentist} falls through the {Trapdoor} of the {Island} clinic and needs a *stand-in*. Her daughter takes over, then her granddaughter, then her great-granddaughter, each **generation** grabbing the drill as the last one retires. By sundown five **generations** of dentists stand in a row, all polishing the same tooth.

The {Ninja} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Lake} cottage into an *inner room*, and **inside** it is another room, and **inside** that another, like nesting dolls. She crawls deeper and deeper **inside** until she reaches a room the size of a shoebox, where a frog is calmly drinking tea.

The {Shepherd} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Inn} beside a *standing person* whose *speech bubble* says: your sheep can fly. The shepherd **believes** it. He tosses a sheep out of the window, and it flaps its ears and soars away. Now the whole inn **believes** every word, and starts **to believe** in flying cows.

The {Baker} goes down to the {Basement} of the {Cat Café} **to show** off her new outfit: a *robe hem* stitched with sequins and a *seedling top* sprouting from her collar. She strikes a pose. The cats **show** no interest. So she puts on a whole fashion **show**, and the cats fall asleep on the catwalk.

The {Hunter} slides out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Water Park} chasing a *shape-shifter*. Every time he grabs it, it **changes**: into a dolphin, an inflatable ring, a lifeguard, a jelly. He splashes after it all day, and in the end the shape-shifter **changes** the hunter into a rubber duck.

The {Lifeguard} rescues an *old man* from the {Basement} of the {Tower}, where he has waited so long his beard wraps round the room three times. He is very **old**: he remembers when the tower was a pebble. She carries him up the stairs while he grumbles that stairs were better in the **old** days.

The {Gardener} sits in the {Basement} of the {Lake} cottage wrapping presents in boxes with *fitted lids*, tied with *silk thread*. She **gives** one to a duck, one to a frog, one to a passing fish. Inside are more presents, which they **give** right back. They **give** and **give** until the basement is a mountain of bows.

The {Sheriff} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and lands on a spinning *globe*, the whole **world** in miniature. He rides it like a bucking bronco while bees zoom round it like satellites. Oceans slosh, mountains wobble, and the sheriff clings on, whooping that he is going round the **world**.

The {Wizard} pops out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Lake} pavilion beside a *podium*, where a *standing person* refuses to leave the top step. Everyone wants that **position**. So the wizard turns the podium into a seesaw, and the **positions** swap up and down every second while the crowd cheers and gets dizzy.

The {Tsar} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and joins a *queue* of bees at the honey tap. The first **time**, he gets one drop. The second **time**, he gets stung. The third **time**, he wears a disguise. Each **time** he rejoins the back of the queue, and each **time** the bees recognise his moustache.

The {Dentist} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Pool} clutching a giant *thermometer* and plunges it into the water. One **degree**, two **degrees**: the water heats up until the swimmers turn pink as prawns. Then she turns it down a **degree** at a time, until the pool freezes and everyone is skating.

The {Magician} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Funfair} haunted house, where a creaking *gate* blocks his way. He taps it with his wand and it becomes a **door**, then another **door** behind it, then a hundred. He opens **door** after **door**, and the very last one opens back onto the same staircase.

The {Robot} rises through the {Trapdoor} of the {Funfair} and becomes the *bearer* of every **responsibility**: it carries the Ferris wheel, the hot-dog stand and three lost toddlers on its back. Someone hands it the keys, the cash box and a goldfish. **Responsibility** piles up until its springs creak and it beeps for a holiday.

The {Chef} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Hangar} under a *hanging lamp* with a frilly *lampshade* that swings and bonks her head. It happens **often**. It happens on every step. She ducks, it bonks; she wears a helmet, it bonks the helmet. It happens so **often** that the mechanics set their watches by it.

The {Shepherd} races up to the {Rooftop} of the {Yen Exchange}, but a *front runner* is already there, wearing a gold medal. '**First**!' she yells. The next day he runs faster: she is **first** again. He sleeps on the roof to beat her, and wakes to find her already standing on his chest, **first** as always.

The {Hunter} goes down to the {Basement} of the {Island} cottage, where a *busy mother* fills buckets with *water drops* faster than he can blink. The buckets overflow, the floor floods, waves rise. Soon the basement is a whole **sea**, with ships and seagulls, and he is paddling a laundry basket across the **sea** to the stairs.

The {Tailor} on the {Rooftop} of the {Lagoon} hotel cuts a *tunnel* with her scissors, a *road* straight down through the building. Cars **go through** the bedrooms, a bus **goes through** the kitchen, a flock of flamingos **goes through** the lobby. Guests complain, but she insists it is much quicker to **go through**.

The {Juggler} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Cat Café} **to teach** her *dutiful son* to juggle, tapping a chalkboard with a *cane*. He drops everything. So the cats **teach** him instead, juggling balls of wool with their tails, and by dinner the son is **teaching** his mother a trick with nine kittens.

The {Ghost} floats up the {Staircase} of the {Car Park} chasing a pair of tiny running *legs*: a **child** playing hide and seek. The ghost has no legs of its own and is terribly jealous. The **child** zooms between the cars, giggling, and the ghost finally borrows a skateboard and gives up being spooky.

The {Yogi} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Mint} and finds a *cliff spring* gushing gold coins straight out of the wall. This is the **original** source: every coin in the world began here. He fills his turban to the brim, only to find the **original** coins are so ancient they have dinosaurs on them.

The {Dentist} wakes on the {Rooftop} of the {Lagoon} lighthouse as the sun bursts up in the *east*, blinding her. Every fish turns to face **east**, every palm tree bows **east**, and her dentist's chair swivels round until it points **east** as well. She brushes her teeth squinting into the sunrise.

The {Sheriff} sits on the {Rooftop} of the {Jungle} treehouse while a *scholar* listens for the strangest **sound** in the forest. He raises one *eyebrow* at every **sound**: a monkey burp, a parrot sneeze, a falling coconut. Then the sheriff's tummy rumbles, and the scholar's eyebrow flies clean off his face.

The {Tailor} struggles up the {Staircase} of the {Beach} chalet with a suitcase full of sand. A *helping hand* reaches down **to lift** it, then **lifts** her too, then **lifts** the whole chalet off the ground. A giant *tick mark* appears across the sky: job done, everything **lifted** and floating.

The {Lifeguard} rises out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Beach} on a *podium* and orders everyone **to stand** up straight. Sunbathers jump up and **stand**. Deckchairs **stand** on their hind legs. Even the sandcastles **stand** to attention. A wave rolls in, soaks them all, and nobody dares to sit down.

The {Juggler} runs up the {Staircase} of the {Beach} pier with a *chaser* just behind her, arm outstretched. He can almost **reach** her. One more step and he **reaches** her hat, then her sleeve. At the top he finally **reaches** her, and she spins round and hands him three flaming torches to juggle.

The {Baker} goes down to the {Basement} of the {Beach} hotel to judge a pair of *twins* in a sandcastle contest. She **compares** their buckets, **compares** their spades, **compares** their freckles one by one through a magnifying glass. Everything is identical. She gives up trying **to compare** and awards both of them a cake.

The {Yogi} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Mint}, where each *employee* wears a badge saying proud **member** of the coin club. The yogi wants to join too. He folds himself into the shape of a coin and rolls past security. They stamp his forehead, and now he is a shiny **member** as well.

The {Juggler} goes down to the {Basement} of the {Yeti Cave}, where the yeti sits weeping in a giant tangle of rope. She juggles the loops until every one is an *untied knot*, puzzle by puzzle. Problem **solved**! The yeti hands her a crossword next, and she **solves** that too, by juggling the letters into place.

The {Sheriff} sits in the {Basement} of the {Waiting Room} when *water* starts trickling under the door. Then gushing. Then roaring. The **water** rises past the magazines and the potted plant, and the patients float about on their chairs. The sheriff lassoes the water cooler, the source of all the **water**, and wrestles it shut.

The {Magician} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Boxing Ring} and slaps a *name tag* on everything: the bell, the gloves, the referee's moustache. Each **name** is sillier than the last: Sir Dingdong, Punchy, Gerald. The boxers refuse to fight until he gives them a better **name**, so he calls them both Champion.

The {Jockey} on the {Rooftop} of the {Funfair} examines every prize through a *magnifying glass*. Is the gold teddy gold? Fake. Is the giant diamond real? Plastic. Is the fortune teller's crystal ball **true**? She peers closer, and it whispers one **true** thing: her horse is eating the candyfloss.

The {Lifeguard} climbs out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Casino} into a meeting where gamblers **discuss** a *neat stack* of chips. Each *small speech bubble* floats up and lands on the pile: 'Mine!' 'No, mine!' They **discuss** and **discuss** until the bubbles reach the ceiling and pop, raining chips on everyone.

The {Chef} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Pool} on *trudging feet*, hunting for the right **place** to have her picnic. A *fortune stick* floats by and points to a **place** at the end of the diving board. She spreads her blanket there, the board bends, and she and her sandwiches are launched into the deep end.

The {Zookeeper} is in the {Basement} of the {Boathouse} when a *runner* sprints past. 'No running! You must **walk**!' The runner slows to a **walk**. Then the ducks **walk**, the boats **walk** out on little wooden legs, and the whole boathouse parades round the basement at a very sensible speed.

The {Yogi} rises through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beach} gazebo, where a *judge* in a curly wig sits on a sandcastle. 'What is the **meaning** of this?' he thunders, pointing at a crab in sunglasses. The crab shrugs. The judge bangs his spade and rules that the **meaning** of life is ice cream.

The {Gardener} lifts the {Trapdoor} of the {Hut}, and a *visitor* climbs out, then another, then a hundred. She hands **each** one a flower, **each** a different colour. **Each** visitor sniffs it, sneezes and climbs back down, and the gardener starts all over again for **each** new arrival.

The {Robot} guards the {Trapdoor} of the {Pool} changing room, beeping at every *person* who wants **to enter**. 'Password?' The swimmers guess: 'Splash?' 'Towel?' 'Verruca?' Wrong, wrong, wrong. Finally a toddler says 'Please', and the robot lets everyone **enter** at once, in a stampede of flip-flops.

The {Juggler} in the {Basement} of the {Beach} house sets a *small table* for dinner, but she doesn't know **how many** guests are coming. Two? Twelve? She juggles plates, adding one every time the doorbell rings. '**How many** more?' she yells, as forty seagulls swoop in, all wanting chips.

The {King} goes down to the {Basement} of the {Boathouse} and finds a giant *mouth* in the wall, wide open, eating rowing boats. The **mouth** crunches oars like crisps. To calm it, the king feeds it his royal sandwich and then his crown, and the **mouth** spits the crown back with a burp: too salty.

The {Robot} pops up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Funfair} and scans every *person* in the queue. It **recognizes** nobody. Then a *small speech bubble* appears above an old lady: 'Hello, tin can!' The robot whirrs, beeps, and finally **recognizes** its inventor. It hugs her so hard she rattles.

The {Tailor} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Cat Café} on *trudging feet*, dragging a *bare tree* behind her. She cuts its bark into long **strips** and hands one to every cat. The cats shred each **strip** into thinner **strips**, and soon the whole staircase is carpeted with curly ribbons.

The {Pirate} stomps up the {Staircase} of the {Boxing Ring} with an enormous rolling pin and rolls everything *flat*: the ropes, the stools, both boxers, the referee. They lie there **flat** as pancakes, blinking. Then the pirate rolls the stairs **flat** too, and slides back down them like a playground slide.

The {Shepherd} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beach} lido onto a *slide* knotted with a *silk skein*. Each tug on the thread opens a gate, tips a bucket and sends a sheep whizzing down another slide. It is a whole **system**, all linked, and when one sheep sneezes the entire **system** goes off at once.

The {Cheerleader} bursts out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Beach} sauna in a cloud of *steam*. She waves her pompoms and the **air** whooshes about, hot and sticky, inflating every lilo on the sand. Beach balls swell to the size of houses. She keeps pumping **air**, and the whole beach floats up like a balloon.

The {Tailor} sits on the {Staircase} of the {Beach} lifeguard station with an exam *page* full of **questions**. Can a crab wear trousers? Do seagulls need hats? She answers each **question** and stitches a *tick mark* beside it in red thread. The last **question** asks her to sew a swimsuit for a whale.

The {Hunter} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Warehouse} and splashes into a puddle of *living water* that giggles and wriggles. Wherever it flows, things start **to live**: crates sprout legs, a broom dances, boxes sing in harmony. The hunter puts down his bow; he would rather **live** here with the singing boxes.

The {Ghost} haunts the {Basement} of the {Car Park} with a tinkling *wind chime*. One thing sets off the next: a car beeps, **so** the ghost jumps, **so** the chime rings, **so** a pigeon panics, **so** the alarm wails. The attendant just shrugs; it is always **so** down here.

The {Gardener} climbs out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Jungle} lodge and bangs a huge *gong*. Every bang makes the plants grow **more**: **more** leaves, **more** vines, **more** bananas. The monkeys beg for **more** bangs. By lunchtime the jungle is so thick that she has to gong her way out.

The {Baker} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Yeti Cave} with a *spare part* for the yeti's oven, past a sign on a *standing knife*: **Don't**! **Don't** touch. **Don't** knock. **Don't** sneeze. The baker sneezes. Avalanche! The yeti whizzes past on a tea tray, yelling '**Don't** say I didn't warn you!'

The {Dentist} in the {Basement} of the {Spa} is hammering a *nail* into the wall to hang a towel. She misses and **hits** her thumb. A *helping hand* grabs the hammer and **hits** the nail, then **hits** every pipe, the boiler and the gong, until the whole spa clangs like a drum kit.

The {Ninja} sneaks into the {Basement} of the {Museum} and finds a marble statue of a *woman*, which suddenly blinks. The stone **woman** steps off her plinth, dusts herself down and challenges the ninja to a race. She wins by a mile, and the guard on the cameras just sees a **woman** jogging past in a toga.

The {Baker} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Yen Exchange}, where a *sweating man* waves his *right hand* over a pile of coins **to change** them. Yen **change** to dollars, dollars to buttons, buttons to bread rolls. The baker grabs the rolls happily, and the man **changes** into a pigeon and flies off.

The {Sailor} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} into a little *fence* pen, where one bee stands on **four** tiny *legs*. It has **four** wings, **four** eyes and **four** stripes. The sailor counts on her fingers, loses her place, and simply salutes it **four** times.

The {Sheriff} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Funfair} to a *small altar* where a tiny **god** in a golden hat sits. Offerings arrive on a *skewer*: kebabs, toffee apples, candyfloss. The **god** eats everything, grows enormous, and starts steering the dodgems with one finger while the sheriff hands him napkins.

The {Zookeeper} in the {Basement} of the {Lagoon} aquarium keeps a *tally* on the wall of every creature: three hundred fish, forty crabs, one grumpy octopus. She adds it all up for the **overall** total, but the octopus keeps rubbing out marks. In the end the **overall** count is: lots, plus one octopus.

The {Hunter} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Hut} under a huge *lotus leaf* umbrella, though it isn't raining. A frog hops out of it: '**What** are you doing?' The hunter has no idea. '**What** is a staircase?' asks the frog. '**What** is a frog?' asks the hunter. They sit on the steps, puzzled, until dark.

The {Dentist} pops out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Yen Exchange} gripping a *lightning bolt* like a drill. **Electricity** crackles everywhere: the tills spin, coins stand on end, the cashier's hair puffs up like a dandelion. She plugs the bolt into the wall, and the whole building fizzes and glows with **electricity**.

The {Sheriff} pops up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Pool} beside a lifeguard with a *tall bun*, who taps each swimmer with a *cane* and shouts a **number**: one, two, three. The sheriff wants a **number** too. She taps his hat: four thousand and six, the biggest **number** of the day.

The {Ghost} floats up onto the {Rooftop} of the {Mansion}, the one *safe home* left in a thunderstorm. Downstairs everything crashes and rattles. Up here it is **peaceful**: no wind, no thunder, just a mug of cocoa. The ghost lies back on the tiles, **peaceful** at last, and stops howling for the first time in three hundred years.

The {Sheriff} in the {Basement} of the {Tower} is cooking chilli for a hundred cowboys, but he has only a *pinch* of beans. A **few** beans: three, maybe four. He shares them out across a hundred plates, so **few** that each cowboy gets a sliver of bean, which they eat very slowly with tiny forks.

The {Baker} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Tower} into a newsroom where a *helping hand* writes and a *pressing hand* stamps every page. They **report** everything: the baker's arrival, his floury nose, the crumb on his lip. Within seconds the whole town is reading a front-page **report** about his breakfast.

The {Tsar} sits on the {Staircase} of the {Island} palace, waiting for a *green shoot* to sprout before he eats his lunch. Day one: nothing. Day ten: nothing. On day forty a tiny leaf pops up, and **only then** does he unwrap his sandwich. **Only then**, and by now it is stale and curly.

The {Juggler} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Yeti Cave} juggling a *lucky charm* tied to a *silk thread*. The thread twists and pulls itself into a giant **knot**. She tries to juggle her way free, but every throw ties another **knot**, until she and the yeti are trussed together in one big fluffy bow.

The {Firefighter} goes down to the {Basement} of the {Mansion}, where a *rebel* does the **opposite** of everything. She says up; he goes down. She sprays water; he sprays lemonade. She shouts stop; he tangos. Finally she orders 'Do the **opposite**!' and the rebel freezes, his brain fizzing.

The {Sheriff} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Boathouse} into the middle of a ceremony: the *handover* of a giant golden oar. He holds out his arms **to receive** it. It is so heavy that he sinks through the floorboards into the river, where he **receives** a second prize: a soggy, outraged duck.

The {Magician} pops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Pool} and pulls an *eye* out of his hat, as big as a beach ball. The **eye** rolls down the steps into the water, blinking. It watches every swimmer, winks at the lifeguard and refuses to close. Everyone swims very carefully under that giant **eye**.

The {Tailor} falls through the {Trapdoor} of the {Island} cottage onto a sleeping *giant*. She tries to sew him a shirt, but he is **too** big. The sleeves are **too** long, the buttons **too** small, the needle **too** short. He sneezes, the island tips over, and she declares the whole job **too** much.

The {Lifeguard} pops out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Stadium} with a measuring jug and tries to measure the *sun*. What **quantity** of sunshine is there? She fills jug after jug with golden light, pouring it into buckets, then bathtubs. The **quantity** never runs out, and soon the whole pitch glows like a pancake.

The {Zookeeper} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Island} cabin and builds a seesaw from a *plank* and a *tortoise shell*. She launches a tortoise into the sky. It lands and says '**Again**!' So she does it **again**, and **again**, until a queue of tortoises stretches all the way round the island.

The {Gardener} chops onions in the {Basement} of the {Mansion} and *tears* stream down her face. She starts **to feel** everything at once: sad, happy, hungry, sleepy. The tears water her seedlings, and they **feel** it too: the roses weep, the tulips sniffle, and the cactus asks for a hug.

The {Juggler} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Yen Exchange} and helps a *builder* **build** a tower of coins. She tosses coins up, he catches them on top, stacking higher and higher. They **build** past the ceiling and past the clouds, until a passing aeroplane has to stop and buy some yen.

The {Wizard} rises through the {Trapdoor} of the {Pool} with a list of every *chore*: scrub the tiles, fish out the plasters, polish the diving board. He waves his wand to do each **task** by magic, but the mop goes rogue and starts scrubbing the swimmers instead. That **task** did not go to plan.

The {Zookeeper} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Warehouse}, where a *storyteller* tells a *standing person* what **to do**. 'Now you lift a crate!' He **does**. 'Now you juggle three hedgehogs!' He **does**. The zookeeper joins in, and they **do** everything the story says, until it ends with a nap.

The {Juggler} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Yeti Cave} as the yeti hurls snowballs at her. A *handmaid* rushes up with a *helping hand* on a long pole, and together they **receive** every snowball, catching them neatly. Then they **receive** a fridge, a sledge, and the yeti himself, who only wanted a hug.

The {Baker} pops out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Beach} kiosk with a *pinned heart* badge listing her rules. She **must** bake a cake. She **must** ice it. She **must** deliver a slice to every crab before the tide comes in. She sprints across the sand, sweating, because the rules are pinned to her heart and she simply **must**.

The {Chef} in the {Basement} of the {Hangar} shovels *soil* across the floor and switches on lamps that blaze *sun rays* everywhere. A whole **field** grows overnight: wheat, cows, a scarecrow. In the morning the pilots find their planes in the middle of a **field**, with sheep grazing under the wings.

The {Juggler} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Yen Exchange}, where a *standing person* is listing every **item** for sale: one hat, one teapot, one *cow*. Each **item** gets a price sticker, even the cow, who eats hers. The juggler buys the lot and juggles them, one **item** at a time.

The {Juggler} pops out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Beach} ice-cream van and must **calculate** the change for a queue of crabs. She juggles numbers out loud, each sum floating up in a *small speech bubble* with a *cross* for every plus. Seven cones, three flakes... She **calculates** so fast that the bubbles pile up and blot out the sun.

The {Gardener} sits in the {Basement} of the {Swan Pond} pavilion, where an *official* with a *bamboo* clipboard is trying **to manage** two hundred swans. He barks orders: swim left, honk quietly, no biting. The swans ignore him. The gardener tosses one crust of bread, and suddenly she **manages** them all perfectly.

The {Cheerleader} sits on the {Rooftop} of the {Beach} chalet timing the *moon* with a *winnowing basket* of sand that trickles like an hourglass. Every **period** the moon goes round, she flips the basket and cheers. New moon, full moon, new moon: each **period** ends with a pompom flourish and a neighbour yelling for quiet.

The {Sheriff} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} into a bustling *market*: bees selling honey, pollen and tiny umbrellas. Stalls spread, streets appear, traffic lights blink. By evening it is a whole **city**, with buses and skyscrapers made of wax, and the sheriff has been elected mayor of the **city**.

The {Jockey} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Beehive} dangling a *plumb line* to check that everything is **straight**. The steps are crooked, so she bends them **straight**. The bees fly wonky, so she makes them fly **straight**. Even the queen's crown is adjusted, and the hive becomes one perfectly upright tower.

The {Dentist} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Hut} following a saint's glowing *footsteps*, while a *watchful heart* on the wall judges her. Every kind act earns **virtue**: she rescues a spider, returns a lost sock, flosses a mouse. The heart glows brighter with each **virtue** until the whole place shines like a lantern.

The {Zookeeper} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Beehive} counting a pile of *shell* money, her **capital** for a new zoo. A *queue* of animals lines up to invest: a monkey brings bananas, a parrot brings buttons. The **capital** grows until she can afford a giraffe, which immediately starts eating the hive.

The {Magician} rises through the {Trapdoor} of the {Boxing Ring} inside a little *tent* with a brass *door knocker*. He knocks once, and a dummy in the corner springs to **life**. He knocks again, and the gloves, the bell and the stools all come to **life** and start a boxing match of their own.

The {Sheriff} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Mansion} as a *mountain* pushes up through the chimney, rumbling. Tiles slide, the roof cracks, and he is lifted higher and higher. Soon the **mountain** has snow on top and goats on its slopes, and the sheriff has to ski down the **mountain** to get back to the front door.

The {Juggler} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Inn} juggling bars of *gold* in the sunshine. Everything a bar touches turns to **gold**: her gloves, the chimney, a passing pigeon, which drops like a stone. The guests rush up to touch the bars, and soon the whole inn is solid **gold** and nobody can open the doors.

The {Jockey} goes down to the {Basement} of the {Beehive}, where a *helping hand* unrolls an *edict scroll* and begins **to point**. It **points** at the honey: yours. It **points** at the wax: mine. It **points** at the jockey: guilty. Every bee **points** too, until she backs slowly up the stairs.

The {King} is trapped under the {Trapdoor} of the {Hut} by a huge *antique* wardrobe sitting on top. He braces his *legs*, pushes and grunts. He must **overcome** it. With one mighty royal heave he **overcomes** the wardrobe and bursts up through the floor in a shower of moth-eaten hats.

The {Shepherd} goes down to the {Basement} of the {Museum}, where a guard grinds a *pestle* under a *small speech bubble* that says: not **allowed**. The shepherd begs and begs. The guard grinds, thinking. At last the bubble flips: **allowed**! And the sheep pour in to graze on the dinosaur.

The {Tailor} sits in the {Basement} of the {Lagoon} aquarium sewing every fish to a *balloon* with *silk thread*. Then she ties all the strings together **to unite** them, and the whole shoal floats up as one. Sharks and sardines, **united** at last, drift out of the window like a single giant kite.

The {Cheerleader} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Museum} waving a huge *district map*, cheering for each **area** as it lights up. 'Go, shopping **area**! Go, picnic **area**! Go, no-pigeon **area**!' The pigeons ignore the signs and land in every **area** at once, cooing smugly.

The {Baker} hides in the {Basement} of the {Tower}, where a fierce *nanny* stands guard over his birthday cake. She will **protect** it from everything: mice, flies, hungry uncles. She **protects** it with an umbrella and a frying pan, and when the baker himself reaches for a slice, she whacks his hand.

The {Jockey} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} just as an *arrow landing* thunks into the floor beside her, with a note: I **arrive** at noon. Another arrow: I **arrive** now! Then a third arrow wobbles in, carrying a tiny bee with a suitcase, who has finally **arrived**.

The {Dentist} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Waiting Room} and organizes her patients into a *team*. They wear matching bibs, pass a toothbrush like a relay baton and floss in perfect time. The **team** wins a trophy shaped like a molar, and the receptionist cheers so hard she joins the **team**.

The {Shepherd} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Boxing Ring} with a *door bar* covered in *bristles* like a giant brush. She sweeps it over the boxers, and each one changes **shape**: a triangle, a star, a squashed doughnut. The referee demands his old **shape** back, but she has already turned him into a square.

The {Sheriff} lifts the {Trapdoor} of the {Hut} and finds a tiny **society** of beetles living around a *small altar* in the *soil*. They have a mayor, a school and a dance on Fridays. The sheriff is invited to join the **society**, but first he has to shrink to the size of a crumb.

The {Baker} discovers a *shortcut* through the {Trapdoor} of the {Yen Exchange}: a slide straight from her oven to the till. How **convenient**! She whizzes down with loaves, swaps them for coins and pops back up in seconds. Soon the whole town uses her **convenient** chute, and the exchange smells of toast.

The {King} climbs to the {Rooftop} of the {Lagoon} castle and opens the door to an *empty room*. Nothing. Not a chair, not a crumb. He shouts, and his echo comes back **empty**. He opens his treasure chest: **empty**. Even the lagoon below has drained, leaving fish blinking on the sand.

The {Juggler} stands at the top of the {Staircase} of the {Ice Rink} juggling *icicles*, unable **to decide** whether to skate. She flips an *archer's ring*: heads, skate; tails, don't. It lands on its edge. She must **decide** right now, so she slides down the banister and crashes into a hockey match.

The {Jockey} rises through the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} onto a *stage* and tries **to govern** the bees. She passes laws: no stinging, buzz quietly. The bees boo and pelt her with *water drops*. She **governs** for exactly one minute, then the queen walks on stage and takes over with a single look.

The {Jockey} goes down to the {Basement} of the {Mansion} and finds a *lying man* stretched across the floor. He **spreads out** his arms, his legs, his newspaper, his picnic. He keeps **spreading out** until he fills every corner, and she has to tiptoe across his tummy to reach the stairs.

The {Magician} in the {Basement} of the {Spa} pulls a *horse* out of a tiny bath towel. The **horse** shakes itself dry, puts on a fluffy robe and slides into the hot tub, neighing happily. The magician tries to make it vanish again, but the **horse** has booked a massage and refuses to leave.

The {King} sits on the {Rooftop} of the {Hut} with a *grain stalk* and a *dipper*, measuring grain like a scientist. Each scoop starts a new **branch of study**: grainology, scoopology, the science of sneezing in dust. He writes a book for every **branch**, and soon the roof is stacked with encyclopaedias.

The {Sailor} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Beehive} with a megaphone, helping a tiny *boss* bee in a suit **to manage** the hive. 'Faster! More honey! Fewer naps!' The sailor salutes and helps him **manage** the workers, until they both realise the queen has been in charge all along.

The {Wizard} goes down to the {Basement} of the {Pool} and unrolls a *spool* of thread with **five** knots. At each knot something pops out: a frog, a duck, a lilo, a mermaid and a very confused accountant. **Five** surprises! The wizard high-fives them all, with all **five** fingers.

The {Juggler} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Beach} lighthouse on a *winnowing basket* packed with *soil*, the **base** of her act. On that **base** she stacks a chair, a ladder, a cat and herself, juggling. The basket wobbles in the wind, but the **base** holds firm, and the crowd below gasps.

The {Yogi} meditates in the {Basement} of the {Mansion} with one *eye* open, and that **eye** gives a *glare* so fierce the bats hide. The butler creeps down with tea: the **eye** glares. A mouse reaches for a biscuit: the **eye** glares. The yogi stays perfectly calm, but that **eye** never blinks.

The {Sheriff} sits on the {Rooftop} of the {Pool} reading a **book** when a *drop* of water lands on the page, then another. The pages swell, and the **book** grows bigger and bigger until it is the size of a raft. The sheriff floats off on it, down the waterslide, still reading.

The {Firefighter} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Lake} lodge as a goose with *spread wings* lands beside her. 'Is this a fire?' she asks. **Not** a fire. 'Is this smoke?' **Not** smoke, just goose breath. Every question gets the same honk: **not**, **not**, **not**. She rolls up her hose and goes home.

The {Zookeeper} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Hut} reading a *rulebook* the size of a mattress. Every step has a **rule**: hop on step three, whistle on step four, never look a penguin in the eye. Then a penguin appears at the top, and the zookeeper breaks every **rule** at once.

The {Tailor} sits on the {Rooftop} of the {Boxing Ring} trying **to listen** to the fight below. A giant *mouth* keeps chattering in her ear, so she raises an *axe* and chops its words in half. Now she can **listen**: punches, cheers, the referee's hiccups. She **listens** so hard her ears grow as big as plates.

The {Baker} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Island} lighthouse covered in flour, and a *white dove* lands on his head. Everything they touch turns **white**: the stairs, the walls, the parrots, the sea. By the top the whole island is snowy **white**, and the baker can no longer find the dove anywhere.

The {Cheerleader} bursts out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Ice Rink} shouting 'Charge!' **But** her team sounds the *retreat*. She leaps forward; they skate backwards. She cheers louder, **but** they skate away faster, until she is cheering alone in an empty rink, **but** still waving her pompoms.

The {Juggler} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Yeti Cave} onto a *rice field* split in two by a painted **boundary**. The yeti glares from one side, a farmer from the other. A *go-between* scurries back and forth carrying insults, until the juggler starts tossing snowballs over the **boundary** and both sides join in.

The {Dentist} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Spa}, which stretches up like a *road* into the clouds. A *big man* in a bathrobe lies across it, snoring. She climbs over him, round him, under him, and finally **reaches** the top, where she **reaches** for a cucumber slice and collapses into the hot tub.

The {Gardener} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Swamp} shack with a lantern full of fireflies, and *light* spills over the black water. Frogs wake, crocodiles blink, lilies open. She shakes the lantern and the **light** floods everything, so bright the swamp becomes a disco and the frogs dance in the **light**.

The {Firefighter} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Hangar} and taps a chalk *square* on the floor with her *cane*. She **puts** everything in it: a plane, a bicycle, a cup of tea, the pilot. They squeeze in tight. She **puts** her own boot in last, and the whole pile topples over.

The {Cheerleader} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Stadium} as a giant *mosquito* blocks the way. She draws a *bow* and fires, but the mosquito is too **strong**: it catches the arrow and bends it like a straw. So she flexes, cheers, and hurls the mosquito clean out of the stadium. Now she is the **strong** one.

The {Juggler} on the {Staircase} of the {Beach} pier meets a *kneeling man* proposing to his true love, **namely** a seagull. The seagull accepts, **namely** by stealing his chips. The guests gasp, **namely** three crabs and a lifeguard, and the juggler tosses the ring high in celebration.

The {Shepherd} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Stadium} beside a *standing person* dressed as an *elephant*: grey suit, flappy ears, a trunk made from a hosepipe. He **resembles** an elephant so well that real elephants come over to say hello. The shepherd puts on ears too, and soon **resembles** one as well.

The {Ninja} creeps up the {Staircase} of the {Mansion} holding a *caught bird* that won't keep still. Sneaking is **difficult**: the bird tweets, flaps and pecks her nose, and every step creaks. It is **difficult**, then more **difficult**, and when the bird bursts into opera at the top, she gives up and lets it go.

The {Cheerleader} climbs a *stepladder* in the {Basement} of the {Yeti Cave}, shouting one excuse per rung. She is late; **moreover**, she is cold. **Moreover**, she forgot her pompoms. **Moreover**, the yeti ate her lunch. At the top rung the yeti points out that, **moreover**, the ladder is his.

The {Cheerleader} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Mint} and plants a *tree* that sprouts golden coins. She raises her *right hand* and announces that she has the **authority** to spend them. The guards salute. She orders cake for everyone, uses her **authority** to make Monday a holiday, and nobody dares argue.

The {Sailor} lies on the {Rooftop} of the {Beehive} staring at a *rice field* below, trying **to think**. Her brain whirs, her *heart* thumps, and thoughts buzz out of her ears like bees. The real bees join in, and soon everyone is **thinking** so loudly that the rice plants cover their ears.

The {Wizard} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Hangar} and finds a *king* using a jumbo jet as his throne. 'I am **king** of the skies!' he declares, ordering the pilots to wheel him in circles. The wizard taps his wand, and the plane takes off with the **king** still sitting on top, waving his sceptre.

The {Shepherd} lifts the {Trapdoor} of the {Stadium} and an *elephant* squeezes out and sits on the centre spot. The match can't start. The **elephant** won't budge for whistles, for buns or for the referee's red card. Finally the shepherd's sheep chase it round the pitch, and the **elephant** scores a goal.
